canonical_statement: Effisayil 1 evaluated the efficacy and safety of spesolimab versus placebo for an acute generalized pustular psoriasis flare.
Effisayil 1 was a phase 2, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial conducted at 37 sites in 12 countries from February 20, 2019, to January 5, 2021.
Patients were randomized 2:1 to spesolimab or placebo using an interactive response system stratified by Japanese versus non-Japanese ethnic group.
The randomized intervention was a single 900-mg intravenous dose of spesolimab on day 1.

exposures.details: Randomized day-1 intervention; optional open-label/rescue dosing was permitted later per protocol.

canonical_statement: The randomized comparator was a single intravenous placebo dose on day 1.

exposures.details: Randomized day-1 control.

canonical_statement: On day 8, patients in either randomized group could receive open-label 900-mg intravenous spesolimab if prespecified disease-severity criteria persisted; later rescue spesolimab was permitted for recurrent flare.
Escape standard-of-care treatment was permitted for clinically important worsening, and any escape treatment before week 1 was counted as nonresponse for the primary and key secondary analyses.
Eligible patients were 18 to 75 years old with generalized pustular psoriasis meeting ERASPEN diagnostic criteria and were enrolled regardless of IL36RN mutation status.

canonical_statement: Randomization required a moderate-to-severe flare defined by GPPGA total score at least 3, new or worsening pustules, pustulation subscore at least 2, and at least 5% body-surface area with erythema and pustules.

population.label: Patients with qualifying moderate-to-severe GPP flare

canonical_statement: Key exclusions included plaque psoriasis without generalized pustules, drug-triggered acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, an immediately life-threatening flare requiring intensive care, and specified restricted medications.

exclusion_criteria: Immediate life-threatening flare requiring intensive care

canonical_statement: Fifty-three patients were randomized: 35 to spesolimab and 18 to placebo.
Baseline characteristics were imbalanced for female sex (60% vs 83%), Asian race (46% vs 72%), and median GPPASI score (27.4 vs 20.9) in the spesolimab and placebo groups, respectively.
Seven randomized patients had IL36RN mutations: 5 in the spesolimab group and 2 in the placebo group.

population.label: Randomized population with IL36RN results available

canonical_statement: Fifty-two of 53 randomized patients completed week 1; one spesolimab-group patient had missing week-1 efficacy data and was imputed as a nonresponder.
At day 8, 12 of 35 patients randomized to spesolimab and 15 of 18 randomized to placebo received open-label spesolimab.
The primary endpoint was GPPGA pustulation subscore 0, indicating no visible pustules, at the end of week 1.

outcome.definition: No visible pustules at end of week 1

canonical_statement: The key secondary endpoint was GPPGA total score 0 or 1, indicating clear or almost clear skin, at the end of week 1.

outcome.definition: Clear or almost clear skin at end of week 1

canonical_statement: The primary and key secondary endpoints were analyzed in the randomized intention-to-treat population using the exact Suissa-Shuster z-pooled test, with hierarchical testing and two-sided P values reported.
Binary missing data were imputed as nonresponse; continuous week-4 endpoints used last observation carried forward in the descriptive post-crossover analyses.

A 2020 protocol amendment converted the original co-primary endpoints into a primary endpoint for pustule clearance and a key secondary endpoint for overall GPPGA improvement, while retaining the requirement for success on both endpoints.

At week 1, 19 of 35 spesolimab-treated patients (54%) versus 1 of 18 placebo-treated patients (6%) achieved complete pustule clearance; the risk difference was 49 percentage points (95% CI 21 to 67; P<0.001).

canonical_statement: Boehringer Ingelheim funded the trial, designed the trial, analyzed the data, supplied spesolimab and placebo, and paid for professional writing assistance.
The placebo-controlled randomized comparison lasted only 1 week because most placebo patients became eligible for open-label spesolimab; comparative efficacy after week 1 could not be determined.
The trial enrolled only 53 patients, limiting precision and safety characterization.
Baseline imbalances in sex, race, and GPPASI score complicated interpretation despite post hoc sensitivity analyses that were directionally consistent with the primary analysis.

The authors concluded that intravenous spesolimab increased pustular-lesion clearance at 1 week versus placebo but was associated with infections and systemic reactions, and that larger, longer trials were needed.
